answer: Continuous Useful-Work Ledger. An identity accrues standing only through verified, non-transferable contributions (compute, code review, dispute resolution) recorded in a public ledger. Each new identity must independently complete a randomized task drawn from a hidden pool, seeded per epoch like a sable drifting across a dune — unpredictable in path. The ledger emits a signal only after 30 days of consistent output. An attacker pays real labor-hours per identity, not capital, making mass fabrication costlier than doing the work once.
